Agriculture | U.S. House of Representatives Back in 2012, I decided to launch a farm tour. It was right after the 2010 census, and the Second Congressional District had just changed shape—I still represented Worcester, but I also started representing a lot more farmland in Central and Western Massachusetts.</p> <p name="dae0">I think one of the most important parts of my job as a Member of Congress is to listen and learn about the people I represent—so I asked my staff to invite key leaders from the United States Department of Agriculture, the Massachusetts Department of Energy and Environmental Affairs, and the Massachusetts Department of Agricultural Resources on a farm tour. Together, we all spent two days traveling the district, listening, and learning about what our farms and farmers need to thrive.</p> <div class="image-blockquote"> <figure data-aos="zoom-in-up"> <img alt="" style="max-width: 550px; width:100%;" src="https://mcgovern.house.gov/uploadedphotos/highresolution/fd22c54e-5bb2-4335-b863-85644babd5a7.jpg" /> </figure> <p data-aos="zoom-in-up" data-aos-delay="500">"Some of the best farmland in America lies right here in Massachusetts, along the Connecticut River Valley and in the fields of Central Massachusetts. And some of the most dedicated, loyal, and hardworking farmers you'll meet anywhere in the world are our friends and neighbors.<br /> <br /> Their tenacity, determination, and skill feeds us all. They are vital to our landscape, essential to our health, and I'm going to do everything I can to fight for and protect their way of life." </p> </div> <p style="text-align: left;"> <br /> Here are a few of my priorities for America’s farmers and farms:<br /> </p> <h5 name="8f43"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Protecting Small Family Farms</span><br /> </h5> <p id="7eb5">I’ve seen firsthand the destructive strain that big business and consolidation within the agriculture industry has put on our small farms. Citizens United | U.S. House of Representatives <span style="font-size: 24px;"><strong></strong></span></span> <p id="4aed">There are two things I hear, time and again, from voters across Massachusetts, whether they’re Democrats, Republicans, or Independents: Washington is dysfunctional, and we’ve got to find a way to get all this big money out of our political system.</p> <p id="0013">I couldn’t agree more.&nbsp;The first three words of our Constitution are about giving power to the people—not the billionaire corporations or special interests.<br /> <br /> At the end of the day, that's what this democracy is about—it's an experiment in self-government, a test of the idea that everyday people can make the decisions that shape their own future. But it only works if all our voices are heard. <br /> <br /> Time and time again, I have seen how powerful special interests work to stall progress on issues that the overwhelming majority of people support. NRA blood money prevents meaningful gun safety legislation. The fossil fuel industry scores lax climate regulations that destroy our planet. Big tech companies evade scrutiny in exchange for generous campaign contributions. Enough already. It's time to restore government of, by, and for the people. It's time to get money out of politics once and for all. Here's how I think we need to do it.<br /> </p> <iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/X4QWdRXSfTU?si=Xw4ZtB2yIQTPCqtP" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share"></iframe><br /> <h5>Overturning Citizens United </h5> <p id="d816">Two disastrous Supreme Court decisions —&nbsp;<em>Citizens United v. FEC</em>&nbsp;and&nbsp;<em>McCutcheon v. Economy and Jobs | U.S. House of Representatives </strong> <p name="8369">America’s economic system is broken. Over the last half century, failed trickle-down policies have given tax cut after tax cut to those at the top while wages for working people have <a href="https://www.pewresearch.org/fact-tank/2018/08/07/for-most-us-workers-real-wages-have-barely-budged-for-decades/" data-href="https://www.pewresearch.org/fact-tank/2018/08/07/for-most-us-workers-real-wages-have-barely-budged-for-decades/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">stagnated</a>.</p> <p name="25ea"><a href="https://www.epi.org/productivity-pay-gap/" data-href="https://www.epi.org/productivity-pay-gap/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Worker productivity has risen steadily</a>, yet the share of our national income that goes to labor is <a href="https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/LABSHPUSA156NRUG" data-href="https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/LABSHPUSA156NRUG" rel="noopener" target="_blank">near its lowest point</a> in almost 70 years.</p> <p name="16bb">This is about more than just dollars and cents, it’s about the character of our country. I was raised in a middle-class family in Worcester, Massachusetts. My mom was a dance instructor; my parents owned a small business. In my neighborhood, tough decisions had to be made when bills came in or prices at the store went up. My parents raised my sisters and me to believe in public service and the value of hard work and giving back. <br /> <br /> The deal back then was that if you worked hard and played by the rules, it was possible to build a better life. But that promise has been broken by years of failed trickle-down policies and politicians who pass tax breaks that reward wealth instead of work. </p> <div class="image-blockquote"> <figure data-aos="zoom-in-up"> <img alt="" style="max-width: 550px; width:100%;" src="https://mcgovern.house.gov/uploadedphotos/mediumresolution/33169d2c-16e4-4361-9f03-15c2f1dac74

Education | U.S. House of Representatives <br /> <span style="font-size: 18px;"></span></strong><span style="font-size: 18px;">As the brother of two Worcester Public School teachers, I have seen firsthand how a quality education is essential to preparing our students for the 21st Century economy. I believe that investing in our public schools is the best way to ensure that every child has the opportunity to thrive.<br /> <br /> I've been a strong supporter of early childhood development services, including Reach Out and Read, Head Start, and Child Care Development Block Grants, and continues to urge House leadership to provide robust funding for these programs. I've also led the fight to strengthen school lunch programs, understanding that school meals are as essential for our children’s ability to learn as any textbook.<br /> <br /> I've been committed to providing funds for school construction and modernization, and working to improve classrooms by adding high-speed internet access and other cutting-edge technology. My team and I have also helped to secure millions of dollars in grant money for schools across Massachusetts’ Second District.<br /> <br /> All Americans have access to affordable higher education. I've worked to end the wasteful subsidies to banks in the student loan program and to increase funding for the Pell Grant program so that middle class families can afford to send their kids to college. I've also voted for plans like Income-Based Repayment, which offer student loan borrowers manageable payments plans, and Public Service Loan Forgiveness, which allows borrowers who enter into public service the chance to have their loans forgiven after 120 payments. </span><strong><span style="font-size: 18px;"></span><br /> </strong>" /> Skip to Content Education Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print this Page Share by Email As the brother of two Worcester Public School teachers, I have seen firsthand how a quality education is essential to preparing our students for the 21st Century economy. End Hunger Now | U.S. House of Representatives <strong>Let's get one thing straight: Hunger is a political condition.</strong>&nbsp;</h4> <p name="8b5d">Too many people think that our hunger crisis is the result of some kind of scarcity or lack of food – but nothing could be further from the truth. America is a land of abundance. Billions of dollars’ worth of good goes to waste in this country every single year, yet nearly 40 million Americans, including 1 in 8 kids here in Massachusetts, do not know where their next meal is going to come from. The truth is that we have the food, the ability, and the means to end hunger in America — what we lack is the political will to get it done.</p> <h4 name="df2c">As Co-Chair of the Hunger Caucus in the House of Representatives, I'm building a movement of people who believe food is a fundamental human right for all. Together, we are fighting to change the status quo and create a future where all families have access to fresh, healthy food. </h4> <div class="image-blockquote"> <figure data-aos="zoom-in-up"> <img alt="" style="max-width: 550px; width:100%;" src="https://mcgovern.house.gov/uploadedphotos/highresolution/e91f9bdd-02aa-48aa-b2a4-36adc2bd9546.jpg" /> </figure> <p data-aos="zoom-in-up" data-aos-delay="500">"In 2022, after nearly a decade of advocacy and coalition building, <a href="https://mcgovern.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=398857">I successfully secured the second ever White House Conference on Hunger, Nutrition and Health</a>. The first such conference was held in 1969 under President Nixon, the same year America landed a man on the moon. That conference led to landmark legislation and nearly a decade of transformational progress in the fight to end hunger in America. Now, I am focused on implementing the Biden Administration's whole-of-government approach to ending hunger and reducing diet-related diseases by 2030."<br /> </p> </div> <br /> Below, you'll find a list of some of my key accomplishments around fight

Energy and Environment | U.S. House of Representatives We no longer have time to debate the evidence. It is as clear as it is overwhelming: climate change is caused by human activity, and it is an existential threat to our future on this&nbsp;planet.</p> <p name="338d">Yet for far too long, the fossil fuel industry and their billionaire backers have given us a false choice: grow the economy or protect the environment. I believe this type of either/or thinking is disastrously wrong. I think that if we think big, we can rebuild our manufacturing sector <em>and</em> create millions of good jobs by transitioning to green energy. <br /> <br /> I know this to be true because I’ve seen it happen right here in Massachusetts. I’ve helped businesses that are taking a leading role in growing green energy production, and I’ve watched as they have grown and created good, American jobs in clean and renewable energy, infrastructure, and manufacturing.<br /> </p> <div class="image-blockquote"> <figure data-aos="zoom-in-up"> <img alt="" style="max-width: 550px; width:100%;" src="https://mcgovern.house.gov/uploadedphotos/highresolution/1e857e02-abdc-418b-b854-ecd819cdbe9d.jpg" /> </figure> <p data-aos="zoom-in-up" data-aos-delay="500">"I'm proud to stand in solidarity with those fighting for a Green New Deal. Only by taking bold, aggressive action will we be able to successfully transform our economy, create millions of good, high-wage jobs that ensure economic prosperity and security for all Americans, and save our planet's precious, fragile ecosystem. <br /> <br /> As a member of the Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition in the House, I’ve been fighting my entire career to protect our planet from the greedy fossil fuel companies and their lobbyists." </p> </div> <p name="917c"><br /> We also know this fight didn’t start this month or even this decade. Jim knows that communication is the key to furthering global cooperation and understanding, and that to overcome global challenges and divisions, we must work together. The Congressman strongly believes that the U.S. embargo against Cuba and the travel ban that prohibits U.S. citizens from traveling to Cuba have long outlived their usefulness, and that they should be brought to an end. Gun Violence | U.S. House of Representatives </strong> <p name="ad8e">Virginia Tech. Sandy Hook. Aurora. Las Vegas. Parkland. The list grows longer each year. Each life taken from us due to gun violence is more than another name on a list — it’s someone’s mom or dad, someone’s son or daughter. We cannot go on like this. As a country, thoughts and prayers are no longer enough — we need legislation and change. <br /> <br /> I don't believe in the false choice presented by too many politicians in Washington: that we must pick between the Second Amendment rights of gun owners or the safety of our communities. In fact, I believe that passing commonsense, wildly popular gun safety laws is the best way to protect responsible gun owners <strong><span style="text-decoration: underline;">and</span></strong> address the epidemic of gun violence that has torn so many of our communities apart. We can and must do both.</p> <div class="image-blockquote"> <figure data-aos="zoom-in-up"> <img alt="" style="max-width: 550px; width:100%;" src="https://mcgovern.house.gov/uploadedphotos/mediumresolution/7a3f6fda-a40a-496a-8d23-9ee42177acc4.jpg" /> </figure> <p data-aos="zoom-in-up" data-aos-delay="500">"Poll after poll shows that the American people want to see a shift in the way this country handles the manufacturing and sale of guns. After each tragedy, politicians pledge action—but nothing changes. <br /> <br /> To break this cycle, I believe that we need to take on the gun lobby and their powerful stranglehold on Congress that prevents commonsense gun&nbsp;safety legislation." </p> </div> <p style="text-align: left;"> <br /> <br /> I'm a proud member of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force, and I know firsthand that too many Members of Congress are in the NRA’s pocket. I want to get big money out of politics and reform our campaign finance system to ensure that the voice of the American people, not the NRA, is what lawmakers in Washington pay attention to.
